chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The fingers of the two hands and the two legs are equal regarding the wergild. For each finger is ten camels, and for the nail is five dinars.

key_terms.إِبِل: Camels (used as a unit of currency/value in traditional fiqh)
key_terms.الدِّيَة: Wergild or blood money compensation for injury or death
key_terms.دَنَانِيرَ: Dinars (gold coins used as a unit of currency)

ai.seo_question: What is the financial compensation for injuring a finger or toe in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of equality in wergild (diyah) across all digits of the hands and feet, a ruling that underscores the uniformity of bodily integrity in Shia jurisprudence. It further distinguishes the compensation for nails (five dinars) from fingers, reflecting the specific valuation of soft tissue versus bone in classical fiqh. This narration is foundational for understanding the detailed calculations of blood money in cases of accidental or intentional injury.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The fingers of the two hands and the (toes of) the two legs are equal regarding the wergild. Regarding each finger is ten from the camels; and regarding the nail is five Dinars’.
